page.layout: One page of text in a single column, with a running head at the top. Below the last line on the right, the secretary's attestation sits beside a decorative flourish, which is not text. The catchword stands at the foot on the right.

main_text.p: Statuimus eundem Joan. Monachum facere in Latinum traduci: ut nostratibus & aliis Chri-stianis, apud quos vigét studia bonarū artium, tot præclara facinora augustorum Imper.inno-tescant. Et si nos nequiverimus, forte aliquis à nobis exortus, vel oriturus, quem tanta hæc gloria manet, pellectus tatarum rerum magnitudine, restituet rem Christianæ Reipublicæ.

Te igitur potissimum ad huius Auctoris traductionem elegimus: quem & in utraq; lingua clarum, & hujusmodi votorum nostrorum, uti Consiliarium nostrum, conscium novimus, & studiosum mandatorum nostrorum, & Joannem Monachum, in obscuro latitantem, Latinis Latinum reddas. Aggredere igitur omine felici, auspiciis nostris, opus hoc præclarum: in quo, præter quod apud studiosos omnes maximè p-mereberis, nobis plurimum satisfacies, & æternitati nominis tui consules; & maximam apud omnes laudem consequeris. Dat. in oppido nostro Gmunden, die 20. Augusti, Anno Domini M. D. XIV. Regni nostri Romani XXIX.

page.notes: The decorative flourish to the left of the signature block is an ornament, not text, and is not transcribed. The printed "2o." for the day was read as "20.". The ligature in "Auctoris" was read as "ct". The printed "Gmunde n," was read as "Gmunden,". Long s was rendered as plain s throughout. Joannem and Joan. were written with j, following the rule for consonantal i.
